judgments.why: Y has the period's dash-laden run-on style and details not on the card (population figures, the Eyck panels in Berlin, Dutch building style), while X adds invented prices, meals and family notes under a modern salutation.
Y reflects his reluctance to travel and worry about home in a style true to the period, while X invents a guide, thaler prices and a broth dinner.
X gushes over Lablache and Fodor with specific observations about the chorus and the applause, while Y is a terse generic summary with invented prices and a complaint about the wine.
Y has the missed 'beautiful, free Englishman', the 'national spirit' irony and a fragmentary ending, while X invents an inn meal, proofs and heat.
Y explains the coupé, intérieur and cabriolet compartments, compares the valley to Dresden and names the play 'List against List', while X invents a hotel, a duck and a colonel.
Y's playful aside that he almost fell in love with Dardanelli and its musical judgments are characteristic, while X invents a Hofkeller dinner and news about Karl.
Y praises the work outright as by 'the greatest master' and names a fourth warrior figure, while X adds modern skepticism, a fee to a keeper and filler about the boys.
X has dense specific detail (the godchildren, Suabedissen's female relatives, Trier on his birthday, 'In Paris I no longer understand German'), while Y is generic with an invented coach fare.
X retells the ballet plot act by act, including the Protestant 'temple' remark and the view from Saint-Cloud, while Y has a sleepwalking man and invented duck and wine prices.
Y has idiosyncratic wordplay about 'Christian' expenses, the 13-and-16 singer breakdown and a rhapsody on Italian singing, while X is a thin summary with an invented friend and Prague.

X continues mid-rhapsody with allusions to Milder, Torelli and the weather prophet Dittmar, and jokes about tipping for the honor of the Prussian professorship, while Y is generic and disparages Eberle.
X is a terse, characteristic fragment ('Also Brussels!', the quill cut 'with a single press', her doubt that he would leave Paris so soon), while Y pads with stew, francs and Karl's grammar.
Y has the Rousseau relics and rose bush, the pilgrim-like donkey rides and plans for Pesaroni and the Louvre, while X invents an inn supper, a fare and news about Karl.

X has rich specifics (the quarter-hour gallery, Saint-Cloud fair compared to Stralau, Lafond 'like a butcher', teasing his wife's liveliness), while Y is generic with invented prices and Immanuel's Latin.

Y has the exclamatory weather lament and the two blossoms with a dedication beyond the card ('one for you, the other for those who themselves have blossomed from this land'), while X invents an inn and students.
X's brief note with the Schiller 'Aranjuez' allusion is authentic in tone, while Y invents kreuzer prices, a Klein daughter, the Karlskirche and Ludwig.
Y reflects on his ill health, the abattoir as Napoleon's legacy and Cousin laughing at his guidebook conscientiousness, while X is generic and invents Cousin as 'insufferable'.
Y is a terse authentic close that mentions Kellermann was present at Stolberg's death, while X invents a ship count, Kellermann's politics, a room price and Karl.
X has expert art commentary (Hemling, Roger, the Correggio 'night', the Boisserée comparison) and the annoying Würzburger passenger, while Y is generic filler.
Y is a terse note with an odd exact time (12:07) and the 'very obliging' Besseling, while X adds an invented meal price, canal lodging and the boys.
X is dated, notes the heat weakening him and the lunch restoring him, and names Mr. O., while Y invents the 'von H.' family, a cold chicken and a florin price.
X has the Prince overhearing him, the estate reaching the Turkish border, the scholars-versus-bankers quip and the Dardanelli/David singing, while Y invents pheasant, prices and snuff.
X has the owls in the moonlight, the students with green oilcloth knapsacks, Windischmann's prayer cure and his wish to travel the Rhine with her, while Y is thin and generic.
Y names the colleagues tentatively (Snell?, Creuzer?), calls them insipid and describes Weilburg's setting, while X invents a kreuzer meal and the boys.
